items.title: Jev + AI Agents: Where a Decision Model Actually Helps
items.summary: Thanks to Neon for making this video possible, check it out here: https://get.neon.com/4dTo3CI Can a harness built around a System One model like TypeSafe's Jev make an AI agent better? I built one on Pi and Gemini 3.8 Flash, pointed it at a messy Postgres database full of traps, and ran 15 tests. items.title: Why Your AI Agents Burn Billions of Tokens (with Tyler Cox and Ish Shah)
items.summary: #agenticai #AItokenomics #localai In Episode #1031, Ish Shah and Tyler Cox (Distinguished Engineers in the Office of the CTO for Dell Technologies' client group) join @JonKrohnLearns to work out why agentic AI bills are exploding and what can be done about it. Over one weekend Ish burned roughly two billion tokens on a side project, and that is the ordinary shape of agentic work now: agents spawn sub-agents, the pie of work grows, and cheaper tokens only invite more ambitious projects. Tyler runs a small Dell lab that pushes hundreds of millions of tokens a day through local hardware instead. In this episode, they define what makes a system agentic, explain how to read a Pareto curve when choosing models, work through the jagged frontier and why most tasks do not need a frontier model, and lay out what moving agentic workloads onto your own hardware does to the economics. items.title: Inside quantum-centric supercomputing
items.summary: One of the biggest misconceptions about quantum computing is that it will eventually replace classical computing, but that’s not the case. *All* quantum computing relies on classical computing, even just for loading data and reading outputs, and many of the most promising quantum use cases involve quantum processing units (QPUs) working alongside the CPUs and GPUs behind powerful classical supercomputers. However, figuring out how these different computing paradigms fit together is easier said than done. In this episode of The Coherence Times, we’re joined by IBM’s Seetharami Seelam and AMD’s Sanjay Chaurasia to explore the emerging world of quantum-centric supercomputing. Together, they discuss the similarities and differences between GPUs and QPUs, explain how quantum and classical systems work together, and offer a glimpse at the next generation of hybrid computing. Learn more about quantum computing and run your first circuits on IBM Quantum Platform → https://quantum.cloud.ibm.com

items.title: Why Deep Learning Failed on Tables for a Decade - Frank Hutter
items.summary: Frank Hutter, co-founder of Prior Labs, on why deep learning struggled with tabular data for a decade: tables are messy and heterogeneous, hyped models like TabNet did not generalise to new datasets, and there was no ImageNet of tables. The breakthrough came from learning to transfer at the level of patterns across many different tables; TabPFN-3.5 now tops the TabArena benchmark. Full interview on MLST: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=72Im-Mm5JKs References: TabNet (Arik & Pfister): https://arxiv.org/abs/1908.07442 TabPFN-3.5 Technical Report: https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17895 #Shorts
